title: Sunny and the Old Banksia Tree | Bedtime Story
description: Join Sunny the quokka as she asks a very old Banksia tree what happens every night in the bush, and the ancient tree gently shows her. A soft, calming tale from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories, perfect for settling little ones down to sleep.
narration:
As the sun began to sink low behind the trees, little Sunny the quokka padded softly through the warm golden light of the bush. The tall grasses swished gently around her, and the air smelled of dry earth and eucalyptus.

At the edge of a quiet clearing stood the oldest Banksia tree Sunny had ever seen. Its bark was grey and deeply lined, like the face of something that had been watching the world for a very long time. Sunny sat down beside it and looked up through its heavy branches.

"Old tree," she whispered, "what happens here every night?"

The tree did not speak with words. But slowly, slowly, it began to show her.

First, the insects settled. The busy humming of the afternoon grew quieter and quieter, and one by one the tiny creatures folded their wings and tucked themselves into the cones and the bark to rest.

Then the stars appeared. Just one at first, a single still point of light in the deepening blue. Then two. Then many, scattered gently across the sky like seeds on the wind.

Then the dew came. Tiny silver drops appeared on the Banksia's long toothed leaves, cool and quiet and soft, each one catching a little piece of starlight.

And then the whole bush grew still. Every creature, every leaf, every root reaching down into the dark earth — all of it breathing slowly, settling, letting the long day go.

Sunny leaned her small head against the old tree's trunk and felt its steadiness beneath her. She understood now. Every night, the bush rested. And so could she.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, old Banksia tree. Goodnight, little one.
